USA.name: United States
USA.measure: homicide deaths per 100,000 (age-adjusted), by race and Hispanic origin

ratio_computed_here.note: Computed here from the two published rates; CDC WONDER does not state a ratio.

USA.source: CDC WONDER, Underlying Cause of Death 2018-2024, Single Race (D158); ICD-10 113-cause list "Assault (homicide)" (*U01-*U02, X85-Y09, Y87.1); queried 2026-10-21
USA.licence: US government work, public domain; CDC WONDER data use restrictions (no re-identification; counts under 10 suppressed).
USA.subnational: Not built: the WONDER API does not allow grouping by state. State-level race rates could be exported by hand from the WONDER web form.
USA.value_note: worked out here: Black (not Hispanic) age-adjusted rate divided by White (not Hispanic) age-adjusted rate

ZAF.name: South Africa
ZAF.note: No current official or peer-reviewed national homicide rate by population group was found. The 2017 national mortuary survey (Prinsloo et al. 2023, PLOS Glob Public Health, CC BY) lists "population group" in Table 1 but publishes no rates by group; its data are available only on request from the SAMRC. Stats SA death-registration microdata (DataFirst) record population group but were not processed here. Older work (Thomson 2004, ISS SA Crime Quarterly 7) gives ranges: African/Black male rates 60–120 and Coloured rates over 60 per 100,000, with Indian and White rates lower but not stated.

_meta.title: Homicide victimisation by race or Indigenous status in six countries
_meta.what: For each of the six countries named on the Destruction page: homicide rates for the minority / historically oppressed group and the dominant group, as each official source publishes them. value = how many times higher the minority rate is, where the source gives (or its two published rates allow) that comparison.
_meta.notes: Each country uses its own categories (US: race x Hispanic origin; England & Wales: ethnic group; Brazil: negros vs não negros; Canada and Australia: Indigenous identity). Where "value" was computed here rather than stated by the source, value_note says so.
